title: Protocol Buffer Deserialization DPU Offloading in the RPC Datapath
problem: RPC serialization/deserialization overhead constitutes significant datacenter CPU tax in microservice architectures. Protocol Buffer deserialization in gRPC adds substantial host CPU consumption during RPC processing.
motivation: Offloading RPC processing to specialized hardware reduces host CPU overhead, improving overall datacenter efficiency and resource utilization.
method: RPC server logic including Protocol Buffer deserialization is offloaded to Data Processing Units (DPUs). The DPU intercepts incoming RPC requests, performs deserialization of Protocol Buffers, and passes processed results to the host where application business logic executes, removing deserialization work from the host CPU datapath.
key_novelty: Offloading Protocol Buffer deserialization to DPUs in the gRPC RPC datapath to eliminate host CPU overhead while maintaining performance parity with traditional approaches.
contributions: Demonstrates feasibility of offloading RPC server logic including deserialization to DPUs
Shows DPU-based RPC offloading achieves performance comparable to traditional host-based methods
Achieves significant CPU usage reduction on the host through RPC offloading
Presents generalizable approach applicable to other RPC frameworks beyond gRPC and Protocol Buffers
